summary: Baseline on commit b30187e (branch bugh): npm run build passes (chunk-size warning only); npm run check passes all 15 dry-build contracts; game is the pass-99 WebGPU capture baseline.

Play/code inspection: gameplay surface is enter->walk/ride->E to talk with 3 NPCs, each with ONE static line (src/main.js npcs). No objectives, no waypoints, no mission state, no save/load (localStorage used only by dev tune UI). No episode-1 systems exist anywhere in src/ despite docs/BACKLOG.md claiming Episode 1 was established with reputation, clue records, and a save schema. BACKLOG's premise is fiction in code.

audit/reports/latest.md = pass 99 (grader gpt-5.6-luna via Cursor picker): visual state is healthy, universal criteria average ~4; visual polish is NOT the largest gap. Discrepancies vs handoff: newest_handoff_prompt.md and High_Country_Game_Handoff/ do not exist (README stale); IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md absent; branch is bugh; docs/BACKLOG.md claims unimplemented Episode-1 systems. Decision: keep pillars, build the loop from actual code reality.

Fresh-critic visual discover pass (independent, fresh context) inspected 32 audit + 32 eye-level WebGPU captures from the CURRENT build (audit/visual-campaign-V0, -V0-eye, 2026-08-29). Top visible deficiency: the sky is a flat three-stop cream/beige gradient with a hard-edged flat white sun disc and zero clouds in all 32 frames; scene fog (bluish 0x9bb4c8) does not match the sky horizon color (cream 0xf0e2c4), so all distant terrain hazes into a color no part of the sky contains. Ranked 1st by player experience over: bare untextured settlement walls, roads as paint stripes, salmon-pink golden-hour wash, placeholder destination props.

R6 before/after capture sets: BEFORE = audit/visual-campaign-V0 (+ -eye, 2026-08-29, pre-change build): flat cream gradient sky, hard-edged flat white disc, zero clouds, bluish fog mismatching sky horizon. AFTER = audit/visual-campaign-V1 (+ -eye, current build): warm amber golden gradient with layered sun (HDR core + halo), blue midday with drifting FBM clouds, fog hue matching sky horizon. 32 audit + 32 eye frames per set; captures regenerated after round-1 self-repair (cloud domain scale, HDR sun core).

Overlook-pose A/B on the aperture-fix build: opaque glass 21/21 fps vs transparent 21/21 fps, identical subset (FPS_POSES=overlook-midday,overlook-golden, fresh preview server, /tmp/fps-ov-transp.json for the transparent side). Glass transparency is causally cleared as the cause of the overlook dips; the steady ~50 ms frame times pin both builds at the same wall, and the pose sat at 21 fps in the full campaign sweep too — 8 fps under the E14-era standalone 29 is measurement-condition variance, not the material change.

Aperture campaign: corral fence found as a closed loop (no collider gap anywhere on its perimeter) while the declared ranch gate is a freestanding range gate ~170 m from it; its old note claimed a fence gap that was never constructed. Note corrected (declared-vs-constructed difference explained, nothing relabelled); the repair itself queued as R8. Observation -> proposed change: gate in the corral fence or documented seal; expected player benefit: fenced paddocks read as enterable horse property, and the range gate stops reading as an unfinished scene; evidence required: collision probe of the perimeter + walk-through of the new gap; decision: proposed as R8, P4.

Door-walk driver root-cause chain (runs 2-5, logs /tmp/probe-doors-run{2..5}.log): (1) steerTo's gain clamp of 60 px/rad sits ~7x under the game's live look scale (~415 px/rad, self-calibrated), so any target approached from more than ~50 deg off-axis lagged the walk forever and the driver ORBITED the target until timeout — fixed with face-first steering (turn in place while |err|>0.9 rad, walk only once facing) and a 620 px/rad gain clamp; partition.west passed immediately after. (2) Successful crossings left the driver INSIDE structures, and the next door's straight approach wedged on interior walls — fixed with a crossing-stack invariant: after every attempt the probe walks back out the way it came (reverse traversal recorded as evidence); barn.front passed after. (3) Long rides freeze mid-heading with perfect aim and dead aim-drag: macOS steals kiosk-window focus mid-run and the occluded window's rAF collapses (~2 fps), which steerTo's progress test misreads as wedging (repo-documented failure mode; see launchOptions comment) — fixed by re-asserting page.bringToFront() every 5 s inside steerTo. All three are probe-infrastructure defects, not world geometry: the offline collision probe of the implicated lines (ranch-to-gate z=300 march, partition through-lines with interiors built) shows displacement 0.00-0.62 at worst, all walkable.

probe lineOf convention: fourth driver defect - probe-doors negated the registry normal (apertures.js: normal points to the exterior; __apertureView verified exterior captures stand at center+normal*d). Offline collision march (/tmp/town-approach.mjs, /tmp/walk-fidelity.mjs, player-fidelity moveAndSlide at radius 0.42 with deck grounding): approach lanes on the +normal side are clear for the town lots; the old lane aimed at the aperture interior and wedged on back walls (sheriff/saloon/store at 6.8m, church door.1 additionally catches a pew row 1m inside). Prior functional side labels inverted; final pass set re-run on the corrected convention (probe-doors run 9, all 31 doors).

run 9 ranch-cluster freeze: with the corrected lineOf the ranch partition/front legs pinned at 21-24m with aim converged and zero displacement. Dry-run marches (which omitted tree/rock/horse/NPC cylinder colliders - src/vegetation.js addCylinderCollider, src/horse.js parked horse, src/main.js npc collider) showed the same lanes clear, identifying un-modelled scatter as the pin environment. Driver remedied for run 10: escalating sidestep ladder in steerTo (0.7s strafes -> 1.3s -> 2s, still A/D real input) plus detour ladder on the staged sibling exterior leg. Run 9 partial log retained; full 31 re-run as run 10.

Run-11 x/z trace diagnosed wedging driver legs as position-state failures, not wall defects: after a PASS the crossing-stack invariant (stack-based) let a leg's wall-hugging approach carry the player INSIDE the bunkhouse, where approach legs pinned on its north interior wall (at=(-379.4,307.4), z 307 wall = bunker north face at 306.8; clearance grid in /tmp/map-blocker.mjs output). Fix in probe-doors.mjs: restoreOutside() verifies 'outside every structure' from the player's physical side-of-plane checks after unwinding the stack (partition exits iterate to the front door; bounded 4 rounds). Run 12 = full 31 on that driver.

Run 12 exposed the third probe-navigation scale: the player wedged on the cemetery's rail line at (-274.6,446.6), 800 m from Silver Creek, and seven successive legs (sheriff/hotel/store/church/saloon doors) died at the same spot — approachAround's sidestep ladder gave detour legs a flat 90 s to cover 780 m, structurally useless at route scale. Fix: far approaches (>60 m) now fall back to the nav graph (window.__navTo(poi,'walk'), same affordance the HUD/minimap advertises); waypoints walked hop-by-hop with drive.mjs steerRoute's closed loop, final 60 m handed to steerTo+the ladder; sidestep recovery legs now distance-scaled. Run 13 = full 31.

Run 13: nav routes FIRED for every far door (e.g. sheriff via Silver Creek: 49 hops/1053 m, elPasoTwoStory 205 hops cross-map — walked hop-by-hop and PASSED) but the cemetery rail line pinned the player at (-274.6,446.6) and wp0 of every route died there too: the shuffle's A/D strafe is perpendicular to FACING, so against a long fence run the player slides ALONG the rail line without ever leaving it (sim: straight lane wedged at (-285.4,446.6) clearance 0.45m in /tmp/pin274.mjs; 15 shuffles = 13 sample d oscillation around the pin). Fixes: (1) drive.mjs shuffles past #3 rotate the facing ~60deg off-bearing and walk a real diagonal so sidesteps cross rail lines instead of sliding along them; (2) approachAround sidesteps anchor 12 m up the lane from the player, not the 400 m midpoint. Run 14 = full 31.

Runs 14-15 (diagonal-escape shuffle): the rotate-walk cleared the fence-pin class but REGRESSED post-pass restores — exits from inside the ranch house/barn now time out (steering ... exit timed out) instead of shuffling out through the door; the rotate-walk inside an interior pin presses the player into furniture faces. Run 13 remains the best full run: 24/31 PASS (every door class), 4 approach-wedge FAILs (ranchGate/sheriff x2/hotel.1), 4 budget-unverified elPaso doors. Next: scope the rotate-walk to APPROACH shuffles only, keep the plain strafe+backoff ladder for restoreOutside exits; run 16 = full 31.

Run 17 (gated diagonal escape + front-door-preferring exits + non-fatal restores): 25 PASS / 2 FAIL, budget then exhausted. NEW passes this run: sheriff.front.door.0/.1 (failed every run since 8 — the diagonal shuffle broke the cemetery-rail pin), hotel.front.door.1, fortGrant.front.gate.0 (1461 m nav ride, 115 hops), elPasoTwoStory.front.door.0 (205-hop cross-map ride, ~2200 m). Remaining FAILs: ranchHouse.partition.east approach timeout (passed staged in run 13) and ranchGate.east.gate.0 (wedged 15 shuffles near (-435,320) despite ladder+diagonal — suspect R8-adjacent real obstruction at the freestanding gate, needs dedicated offline march). Unverified by budget: 4 elPaso doors -> run 18 is HC_ONLY for exactly those.

nav routeTo snap leg: pose→first-node leg was never collision-sampled, so routes opened at a nearest node the rider could not actually reach — run 17's route to ranchGate opened with a straight hop through the barn walls (pinned the driver 11 legs); offline repro: nearestNode from (−426.9,325.6) returned node 83 whose legClear=false; fix: nearestNode clearFrom option prefers the nearest node the pose can WALK to (legClear, 8-candidate scan), regression-guarded as check-approaches rule 11

probe outside-invariant: door-plane side tests cannot distinguish inside from beside-a-wall (run 17 exits physically succeeded every round yet the single-plane test alternated behind barn.front/barn.right and burned the whole guard, then every later leg started inside the barn). Fix 1: containment comes from the game's own footprint index via new read-only window.__insideStructure hook (kit.js insideStructure, pad 0.5); offline validation: 12/12 probe points agree including the run-17 pin and the 5m-outside-front-door false positive. Fix 2: nav fallback in approachAround benefits from the E27 snap-leg fix so route openings no longer cross the barn

run 19 (both probe fixes in, fresh build): ranchGate.east.gate.0 PASSED — closes the 31/31 union of traversable doors walked through closed-loop (runs 13+17+18+19; no budget orphans). partition.east approach wedged as in every full run (13's staged walk-through remains its evidence). Inventory-identical-after-save/load PASS (67 ids). Logs: audit/evidence/probe-doors-run{17,18,19}-2026-08-31.log

R9 created and activated (operator-directed): observation -> the two figures the player most often sees are primitives; the third-person player is a capsule+hat with no limbs or animation, NPCs are colored capsule+head, and the mounted figure is never seated on the horse. Proposed change -> shared procedural figure kit (src/figures.js) dressing player and NPCs with per-figure variation, procedural walk/idle motion, and a seated rider pose. Expected player benefit -> dialogue, travel and the chase cam look at people who look like people (P2, P6). Evidence required -> before/after captures (ranch third-person walk, dialogue close-up, mounted third-person), npm run check + build, frame-time spot check, independent fresh visual critic. Decision -> scope confirmed with the operator: player + NPCs + seated mounted rider, figures with motion (over player-only and geometry-only); R9 status active, work starting now.

R9 accepted: the third-person avatar and mounted rider are now dressed 1880s figures with a procedural stride from the shared figure kit (src/figures.js). Player yaw converts through headingRotationY so the +Z-fronted figure faces travel; NPC facing measured 0.0 deg error, player front-dot-travel 1.000 at spawn and 0.993 at yaw 45 deg; mounted rider front-dot-horse-head 1.000 with seated hips. Dialogue opens on a three-quarter two-shot framing both figures. Frame time improved (39-60 FPS vs 13-17 before).

Backlog candidates from the R9 critic review (both judged out of R9 scope): the untextured capsule horse is now the roughest object in its frame next to the dressed figures (candidate for a horse-model requirement), and NPC figures read as featureless at dialogue range where their faces meet the camera (candidate for facial detail). Recorded so the next campaign selection can rank them.

R10 accepted: the horse is now a jointed animal - chest/barrel/haunches with saddle at the rider-seat topline, withers-pivoted neck carrying the head at ~1.9 m, mane and tail, four two-joint legs whose gait crossfades a lateral walk into a rotary gallop by speed with knee fold, suspension and body rock, plus idle weight shift/tail sway/ear flicks. The old rig's legs wobbled sideways because they swung about the X axis; the +X-forward animal swings about Z. Rig is a named pivot hierarchy on the same update(dt, speed) contract as the figure kit, so a future skinned model maps joint-for-joint. Fresh critic ACCEPT with no new defects; frame time 37.4 -> 32.5 ms on the ranch vantage.

Backlog candidates from the R10 critic review: (1) head-yaw turn lead on the horse is +0.013 rad, effectively imperceptible - a larger lead coefficient would read better; (2) gallop visual evidence via abeam capture is unreliable because moveAndSlide bends the gallop path around obstacles - a scripted straight-gallop stretch (e.g. the range trail) would make future gallop frames captureable.
